artworks.title: Rhea Presents the Swaddled Stone to Cronus (relief)
artworks.description: Roman-era relief depicting the pivotal trick of the succession myth as told in Hesiod's Theogony. Rhea hands her husband Cronus a stone swaddled in cloth in place of the newborn Zeus; the deceived Titan swallows the stone, and the future king of the gods is spirited away to be raised in secret.

popCulture.title: Rhea (moon)
popCulture.description: Saturn's second-largest moon took the Titaness' name — Rhea orbiting the Roman Cronus, mother of gods among the rings.

popCulture.title: Rhea (mythology)
popCulture.description: The mother who hid Zeus from Cronus remains the mythic type of the protective parent — Rhea as the stone in the swaddling clothes.
